sections.statement: A surgeon who trained as both dentist and physician — bringing a full medical education to the management of anesthesia, trauma, and the complex cases other clinicians refer out.

sections.title: Two doctorates, one surgeon.
sections.sub: What sets Dr. Vahedi apart is not a single degree but two — a full dental education and a full medical education, earned in sequence.

nodes.detail: B.S. in Molecular, Cell & Developmental Biology.

nodes.inst: Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry, USC

nodes.detail: Doctor of Medicine (MD) from the College of Medicine, followed by residency in Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery at the University of Nebraska Medical Center.
Led the oral and maxillofacial surgical service as Chief Resident.
Diplomate of the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery.
Listed in the hospital's own provider directory.

sections.title: The full scope of oral & maxillofacial surgery.

rows.d: Management of facial injuries and fractures.
Corrective jaw surgery to restore function and alignment.
Evaluating and addressing conditions of the mouth and jaw.
Removal of impacted and problematic third molars.
Single, multiple, and complex implant reconstruction.
Bone grafting and ridge augmentation to rebuild lost support.
IV sedation and general anesthesia, managed with a physician's training.

sections.title: The cases you refer out, received by a surgeon trained as a physician.
sections.sub: A surgical practice lives on referrals from general dentists and orthodontists. When a case calls for judgment beyond the general chair, Dr. Vahedi's dual training — dentist and physician — is the reason to send it here.

items.d: Single, multiple, and complex implant reconstruction with bone grafting and ridge augmentation.
Impacted third molars and the extractions better handled surgically.
Corrective jaw surgery, facial trauma, and fracture management.
IV sedation and general anesthesia, overseen with full medical training.
Evaluation of conditions affecting the mouth, jaw, and surrounding structures.
